subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should the bundled WhatsApp plugin replace Baileys multi-file auth with a plugin-owned SQLite-backed store now, and what supported migration, recovery, and rollback contract should existing linked sessions receive?
rationale: The decision sets the durable storage model for sensitive authentication and Signal keys, including whether and how existing on-disk sessions migrate without breaking status, logout, recovery, or upgrades.

options.title: Sponsor a plugin-owned SQLite migration
options.body: Adopt a single canonical SQLite auth store with a doctor-owned one-time migration from the shipped multi-file layout and focused upgrade/recovery proof.

options.title: Keep hardened multi-file storage for now
options.body: Retain the current file-backed design and scope follow-up work to concrete corruption or startup failures while postponing the storage-model migration.

options.title: Prototype behind an explicit migration plan
options.body: Ask for a narrowly scoped design or PR that proves the migration contract before accepting a permanent storage replacement.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a plugin-owned SQLite migration
recommendation.body: Adopt a single canonical SQLite auth store with a doctor-owned one-time migration from the shipped multi-file layout and focused upgrade/recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent auth persistence and recovery work makes this the closest available ownership signal for the migration contract.
